summary: Phase S1 passes public API and package-DX review: all 30 declared package-specifier exports resolve and load, every declaration/runtime target exists after build, package metadata and scripts are consistent, and no app-private or legacy package-scope coupling remains.
nonblocking_findings: S1-API-001 [medium]: srs-engine and practice-core have no package-root README, so their standalone consumer guidance is weaker than knowledge-space-core and knowledge-space-practice. Add package-root usage/API documentation during the Phase S4 governance/documentation work rather than changing the mechanical S1 import.

S1-API-002 [low]: All four packages remain private at version 0.1.0. This is appropriate for the current workspace import, but publication/version compatibility remains intentionally deferred to Phase S4.
evidence: Focused import/boundary/build-export contract passed 10/10 at baseline 60397049.

A consumer-style Node probe imported every export using its public @reading-advantage package specifier: 8 knowledge-space-core, 5 knowledge-space-practice, 7 srs-engine, and 10 practice-core exports (30 total).
Every manifest export has an existing built import target and declaration target, and the focused contract dynamically imports each runtime target.
All manifests consistently declare type=module, matching main/module ./dist/index.js, root types ./dist/index.d.ts, files=[dist], and build/check-types/lint/test scripts.
No @math-platform package names, app source paths, or app-private entrypoint coupling were found in the reviewed manifests and consumer documentation.

Knowledge-space-core and knowledge-space-practice retain package-root READMEs; practice-core retains generator-specific documentation but no package-root README; srs-engine has no package-root README.
Conditional exports preserve distinct runtime and declaration targets, and the dependency-boundary contract verifies production package imports are declared.
